AMERICA READS/COUNTS 
America Reads, a national literacy campaign initiated in 
1996, challenges every American to help children learn to 
read independently. America Counts, launched in 1999, aims 
to improve young students' achievements in mathematics. 
Studies indicate that children who do not achieve a third- 
grade reading level by the end of third grade often fall 
behind their peers, making early intervention crucial. At 
UMass Dartmouth, the America Reads/Counts program 
connects university students with local community centers 
and elementary schools to provide classroom support, 
tutoring, and mentoring for local youth. 
Over the past year, 68 UMass Dartmouth students served 
in classrooms and afterschool programs at 5 locations in 
Fall River and New Bedford, including: Bay Village Housing 
Authority, Boys & Girls Club of Fall River, Boys & Girls Club 
of New Bedford, Henry Lord Community School, and 
Presidential Heights Housing Authority. Providing 4,161 
hours of tutoring to over 545 youth. This marked the second 
year of our Peer Leader Program, with five students serving 
in leadership roles across our sites. They provided critical 
support to fellow tutors, contributed to the successful 
implementation of the program, and acted as key liaisons 
between the University and our partner sites. 
Over the program’s 28-year history, an estimated 2,897 
students have contributed over 581,500 hours of tutoring to 
over 22,000-grade school students in our region.
